title: Point architecture at the truthcv package layout (post Phase 1-5 refactor)
rationale:
Phases 1-5 (PRs #223-#228, main c217dd0) moved every Python package under one truthcv/ package and renamed jobs to background_tasks. Behaviour is unchanged.

Only description text changes here, and only for the 26 components listed. The other 6 (web-ui, truth-data-volume, llm-provider-service, prompt-store, application-agent, job-feeds) are left out because nothing in them is stale, and they stay as they are. No connection changes: the drift decisions already applied them. Every widget, tech list, route table and schema is carried over unchanged except for the text fixes below.

What changes:
(1) Old code paths in 16 descriptions now name the new truthcv/ paths. Examples: api/ → truthcv/adapters/http/, truth/ → truthcv/domain/truth/, jobs/ → truthcv/infra/background_tasks/. URL paths (/api/...) and data file names (truth.yaml, applications.json) do not change.
(2) API: the description says handlers are now thin and the Services Layer orchestrates. It also describes the per-resource route modules, the schemas/ package, and the MCP mount (the one allowed import between the adapters).
(3) Secret Store: corrects a statement that was wrong before this work. It gets data_dir from Storage, not from truth.store.
(4) 10 components that had no description get one: onboarding-store, company-research, run-store, keyword-vocabulary, browser-service, storage-leaf, services-layer, gmail-response-sync, identity-leaf and mcpschema-leaf.
(5) Job Runner is renamed to "Background Tasks" to match the new package name. Its id stays job-runner.

After approval, the generated docs (docs/architecture/**, plus the generated blocks in docs/domain/glossary.md, docs/reference/api.md and docs/reference/data-model.md) should be regenerated from the canvas.

data.text: FastAPI backend (truthcv/adapters/http/) that serves the static React bundle and exposes the wizard REST routes. Its route handlers only parse and validate input, call one Services Layer function and translate the result to HTTP; the Services Layer orchestrates the pipeline: PDF upload → truth extraction → job tailoring → guardrail validation → render/download. Configured entirely from env / .env at container start (no secrets entered in the UI). Routes are split into one module per resource (truthcv/adapters/http/*_routes.py) and registered in match order by truthcv/adapters/http/routes.py; request and response models live in the truthcv/adapters/http/schemas/ package. The same process mounts the MCP tool surface from truthcv/adapters/mcp/, the only permitted import between the two adapters.

data.text: POST /api/render accepts optional approvals:{approvedClaimIds[],deniedClaimIds[]}. On a guardrail block it returns blockedClaims:[{claimId,experienceId,text,tokens[]}] — each a whole draft bullet that tripped the guardrail. Approving a claim makes its text allowed for THAT render only (merged into the matching scope's allowed set before truthcv.engines.guardrail.validate); denying drops the bullet from the rendered draft. Approvals must NOT be persisted to truth.yaml (write_confirmed is NOT used here) because the user generates many tailored CVs/cover letters from one immutable truth file. claimId is a deterministic hash of experienceId+text so the frontend can round-trip decisions.

POST /api/confirm-inferences accepts approved:[{id, claim, experienceId}] so a user-edited claim (and re-targeted experience) at Step 4 is what gets written as the user-confirmed bullet. approvedIds:[string] is still accepted as a deprecated fallback (writes the original draft claim). write_confirmed persists the supplied claim text verbatim.

data.text: POST /api/render and POST /api/cover-letter accept an optional applicationId. When present, the rendered output is saved as the named application's owned CV/cover-letter document (per-application filenames, e.g. cv_<appId>.pdf) instead of overwriting the shared cv.pdf/cover_letter.pdf. Absent applicationId preserves today's behavior (scratch preview files). Applications may have no posting (General submissions).

POST /api/render returns the rendered CV HTML as `html`, and POST /api/cover-letter returns the generated letter as `text`. These expose the generated content so the Web UI can pre-fill an editor; the user edits and saves it back via the guardrail-checked PUT /api/applications/{id}/cv (html) and .../cover-letter (text) routes.

When attaching a document to an application (PUT /api/applications/{id}/cv, PUT /api/applications/{id}/cover-letter) or rendering to an application (POST /api/render, POST /api/cover-letter with applicationId), the guardrail runs first and the document SOURCE is saved before rendering. If WeasyPrint (PDF) and pandoc (DOCX) are both unavailable, no file is produced and download URLs are null — but the save still succeeds. Responses carry renderUnavailable:true in that case so the UI can report "saved to the application, but its PDF/DOCX couldn't be generated in this environment (install the render backend / run the Docker image)". Do NOT treat renderUnavailable as a save failure.

POST /api/cover-letter accepts an optional approvals:{approvedClaimIds, deniedClaimIds}. Approved claim texts are added to the guardrail's allowed set for THIS generation only (no truth.yaml write); denied claims are dropped before rendering. When blocked, the response returns grouped blockedClaims:[{claimId, text, tokens}] (same shape as POST /api/render) so the UI can offer per-claim approve/decline and re-check, instead of only a flat unverifiable token list.

components.name: Truth Store

data.text: Owns truth.yaml, the single origin of all facts (truthcv/domain/truth/). Extracts text from an uploaded CV in any supported format — PDF (pypdf), DOCX (python-docx), TXT or Markdown — and builds, validates and persists the structured truth file (every role/company/date/bullet/skill tagged source:uploaded-cv with a stable id). The LLM step that turns that text into a truth file lives in the Services Layer (truthcv/services/truth_extract.py), so truthcv/domain/truth/ imports neither prompts nor providers. Legacy entries tagged linkedin-pdf remain valid. User-confirmed inferences are tagged user-confirmed.

Hobbies (truthcv/domain/truth/model.py Hobby) are extracted from the uploaded CV as a standalone hobbies[] list, guardrail-validated like any other fact, and used by the Cover Letter Engine only — never rendered into the CV.

components.description: Owns truth.yaml, the single origin of all facts (truthcv/domain/truth/). Extracts text from an uploaded CV in any supported format — PDF (pypdf), DOCX (python-docx), TXT or Markdown — and builds, validates and persists the structured truth file (every role/company/date/bullet/skill tagged source:uploaded-cv with a stable id). The LLM step that turns that text into a truth file lives in the Services Layer (truthcv/services/truth_extract.py), so truthcv/domain/truth/ imports neither prompts nor providers. Legacy entries tagged linkedin-pdf remain valid. User-confirmed inferences are tagged user-confirmed.

data.text: Tailors a CV to a specific posting (truthcv/engines/tailor/). Extracts the posting's keywords/requirements via a provider, then selects, reorders, and rephrases ONLY entries referenced by id from truth.yaml. Detects any claim the LLM wants to add that is not already in the truth file and surfaces it as an approval checklist (confirm-inferences step); nothing unapproved reaches the CV.

The core truthfulness guardrail (truthcv/engines/guardrail/): a pure, deterministic, scoped token-diff of a draft against truth — no LLM. validate(scopes, global_values) returns ok plus BOTH a flat unverifiable[] token list (back-compat) and structured blocked_claims grouping untraceable tokens under the specific source text (bullet) and scope id they came from, so callers can present whole-claim approve/deny. A token is verifiable if it is a stopword or appears (post-tokenization) in its own scope's allowed set (or the caller-supplied global_values — global skills for CV renders; for cover letters the Cover Letter Engine passes every truth value, including hobbies and the profile header, since a letter weaves the whole career). Render-scoped approvals are passed in by merging an approved claim's text into that scope's allowed set for a single render — the guardrail itself never mutates truth.

The Profile summary is validated in its own Scope against the truth/source, exactly like a bullet — an edited summary that introduces tokens not in the Truth File is blocked at render. Profile identity fields (name, email, phone, location, links) are NOT claims and are exempt from validation; never tokenize them into a guardrail scope.

Renders the approved CV from one Jinja-templated ATS-safe HTML source (truthcv/engines/render/): PDF via WeasyPrint (pure-Python, single column, selectable text) and DOCX via pandoc. Runs an ATS linter before download that warns on multi-column layouts, tables, text-in-images, non-standard headings, missing contact block, and posting keywords absent from the CV. No LLM dependency.

Thin LLMProvider abstraction (truthcv/integrations/providers/) with three implementations — anthropic | openai | ollama — selected by the LLM_PROVIDER env var. Interface: complete(system, messages) → str and extract_json(system, messages, schema) → dict. Adding a provider later = one new file; no truthfulness logic depends on which provider is active.

Guardrailed cover-letter generation (truthcv/engines/coverletter/). build_letter() asks the LLM (via the provider layer) for a cover letter as tagged paragraphs, each declaring the factual claims it makes. Every claim is validated by the Guardrail Validator against the Truth Store; if any claim is unverifiable the letter is BLOCKED (returns {blocked: true, unverifiable, text: ""}). Otherwise the paragraph text is joined and handed to the Renderer for HTML/PDF/DOCX output. Serves /api/cover-letter together with truthcv/engines/render/.

Neutral encrypted credential/secrets vault (truthcv/infra/secretstore/), extracted from the API to break the api↔providers import cycle. Resolves LLM credentials — reading data/secrets.enc (Fernet, gated on ENCRYPTION_KEY) and falling back to environment variables — and persists them via atomic tmp-rename. A leaf that uses Storage (truthcv.infra.storage data_dir) only for the data path. Depended on downward by both the API and the LLM Provider Layer.

Owns the user's job-application records (truthcv/domain/applications/) persisted as applications.json on the Truth Data Volume. Each Application tracks a submission (Company, Website, Application URL, Submitted, Submission Type, Reached Out, To Who, Response Received, Method) and OWNS its generated documents: an editable CV and cover letter saved per-application (so old outputs are retained and traceable to the application they went out with). Applications may exist WITHOUT a job posting (General/portal submissions). CRUD helpers use atomic writes mirroring truthcv/domain/truth/store.py; re-renders edited document content via the Renderer.

data.text: External Google service used for the Gmail connection: the OAuth 2.0 browser flow (accounts.google.com authorize, oauth2.googleapis.com/token for the PKCE code exchange and refresh-token renewal) and the Gmail REST API (gmail.googleapis.com/gmail/v1/users/me/profile) read to identify the connected mailbox. Reached over HTTPS with httpx from truthcv/integrations/connections/auth/gmail.py; tokens are persisted via the Secret Store.

Provider connection layer (truthcv/integrations/connections/): a static catalog of connection cards plus per-vendor auth flows. Claude Pro/Max signs in with a PKCE paste-code flow; ChatGPT (OpenAI) signs in with an OAuth device-code flow; Gmail uses Google OAuth 2.0 PKCE. Tokens are persisted encrypted in the Secret Store and refreshed lazily on use.

fields.notes: Offline refresh token; carried over when Google omits it on refresh.

fields.notes: Refreshed lazily once within 300s of expiry.

data.text: Owns the unattended agent's configuration (truthcv/domain/agentconfig/): autonomy mode, schedule, company blocklist and watchlist, cooldown windows, job search profiles, and the global list of job boards the agent searches. Four default boards are always part of that list and cannot be removed, but any board (default or the operator's own) can be switched off, and a disabled board is not searched. Also composes the deterministic dork-style search queries handed to each run (titles, locations, remote terms and recency only; rejected role types are enforced by screening, not search), and supplies built-in search/posting URL presets for known direct boards.

fields.name: job_boards[].source
fields.notes: A catalog key (linkedin, ashby, greenhouse, lever, personio, workday) or a raw domain.

fields.name: job_boards[].signin_url
fields.notes: Operator-supplied sign-in URL; blank for a known board, which resolves from the catalog.

fields.name: job_boards[].mode
fields.notes: dork | direct. User-settable only for custom boards (source not in the boards.py catalog). Catalog boards derive a fixed mode and ignore any stored value. Defaults to dork on load for backward compatibility, and to direct for a newly added custom board.

fields.name: profiles[].title_keywords
fields.notes: Job titles used to compose Google dork queries. When empty, titles are detected from keywords by title noun (Engineer, Developer, Analyst…), falling back to the raw keywords. Each dork is capped at 32 words and split into several queries per board when needed.

fields.name: job_boards
fields.notes: The operator's OWN boards. The four default boards are unioned in at resolve time and are stored here only when carrying a signin_url override or when disabled.

fields.name: job_boards[].enabled
fields.notes: Defaults to true. False keeps the board listed but excludes it from dorks, direct boards and API feeds. Applies to default boards too.

fields.name: dork_recency
fields.notes: Recency as an after:YYYY-MM-DD operator in composed dork queries; default w (past week); camelCase dorkRecency

data.text: Screens discovered postings against the active job profile's criteria and records the verdict. Owns the hard-criteria validators (truthcv/domain/screening/criteria.py): a posting's stated remote arrangement and any explicitly required working language are checked against the profile's remote_model / working_language, and the evidence is stored on the Screening record alongside the profile it was judged against.

First-run onboarding state (truthcv/domain/onboarding/): records which setup steps are complete, such as a provider being ready and a CV profile existing, and persists it on the Truth Data Volume through Storage. The API reads and updates it through truthcv/services/onboarding.py.

Company research findings (truthcv/domain/companyresearch/): structured claims about a company, each with a claim type and source class, keyed by the company identity key from the Identity Leaf. Tracks superseded claims and open contradictions, which screening consults. Persisted on the Truth Data Volume.

Records of unattended agent runs (truthcv/domain/runs/): run lifecycle and status, counters, discovery coverage, and the per-run URL ledger with its channels and outcomes (truthcv/domain/runs/url_ledger.py). Persisted on the Truth Data Volume; only the most recent runs are retained. Run guards and the source funnel live in truthcv/services/runs.py and funnel.py.

fields.name: boardBreakdown
fields.notes: Per job board (from screening URL host): postingsSeen, forReview, rejected

fields.name: discovery_coverage[].tier
fields.notes: Which extraction tier produced the postings: api, harvest, llm, or empty when not applicable.

fields.name: discovery_coverage[].status
fields.notes: searched | empty | blocked | login_walled | skipped. 'blocked' means the page was unreadable (CAPTCHA/consent/bot wall), distinct from 'empty'.

fields.name: finish_refused
fields.notes: Set when finish_run was refused once for incomplete direct/dork discovery coverage; the second call always records.

data.text: Keyword vocabulary (truthcv/engines/vocabulary/): the shared keyword data used by tailoring, the guardrail and the renderer's ATS keyword check, persisted on the Truth Data Volume.

The containerised headful Chromium (browser/ container, served by @playwright/mcp). The Application Agent drives it over in-network HTTP MCP. The API reads, opens and closes the operator browser session through its session-control endpoint via truthcv/services/browser.py.
Lowest-level file storage (truthcv/infra/storage/): data_dir() resolution (DATA_DIR, default ./data) and atomic, locked file writes used by every store. Imports nothing first-party.

All business logic (truthcv/services/). Both adapters, the HTTP API (truthcv/adapters/http/) and the MCP tool surface (truthcv/adapters/mcp/), parse input, call one service function, and translate its result or a services.errors exception into their wire format. Services never import the adapters or FastAPI, and receive the LLM provider (or a provider factory) from the caller. The layering is enforced by import-linter in pyproject.toml.

External third-party Jev (TypeSafe) service at https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone. Screening posts job-posting text to it for hard-requirement cross-checks (truthcv/domain/screening/jev.py), invoked from the agent tool surface (_evaluate_jev_criteria) and the API's check_key route.

Matches Gmail replies to tracked applications (truthcv/domain/gmailsync/): reads the connected mailbox through the Gmail connection, produces response suggestions, can cross-check them with Jev, and records accepted ones on the Application Tracker. Runs on demand or as a background task.

Bounded background job executor (truthcv/infra/background_tasks/): a shared thread pool (MAX_WORKERS=4) plus an in-memory, thread-safe registry of Job records. Callers submit a zero-argument callable via submit(kind, fn); it runs on a worker thread and its outcome (result or exception) is recorded on the returned Job. get()/list_jobs() poll registry state. Registry is in-memory only - jobs are not persisted across restarts.

fields.name: kind
fields.notes: caller-supplied job kind, e.g. gmail sync, feed refresh

fields.name: status
fields.notes: pending | running | done | failed

fields.name: progress
fields.notes: caller-defined 0..1 fraction, default 0.0

fields.name: result
fields.notes: set only when status=done

fields.name: error
fields.notes: set only when status=failed

data.text: External public Arbeitnow job-board API (https://www.arbeitnow.com/api/job-board-api). Job Feeds (truthcv/domain/jobfeeds/arbeitnow.py) fetches paginated postings from it on every feed refresh, because arbeitnow is a default, non-removable board (truthcv/domain/agentconfig/boards.py).

Stdlib-only identity helpers shared by every layer (truthcv/infra/identity/): company identity keys and name validation (company.py) and posting-URL validation, normalisation and dedupe keys (url.py). Imports nothing first-party.

Stdlib-only MCP input-schema builder (truthcv/infra/mcpschema/): derives each MCP tool's JSON input schema from its Python signature. Used by the MCP tool surface and by the API's MCP endpoints. Imports nothing first-party.
